newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to hold election census in November.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to hold election census in November.

text.p: Turkish MPs have approved plans to hold a national census in November in preparation for early general elections, parliamentary officials said on Thursday.
They said parliament passed a bill on Wednesday night outlining a door-to-door population count on November 30.
Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz has said he wants early polls by next spring but he has fixed no definite date. Elections would normally be due by the year 2000.
A leftist party that gives key backing to Yilmaz's minority coalition this week dropped demands that the government go to the polls before the end of this year.

The Islamists of former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan narrowly won the last general elections in December, 1995, but their coalition with conservatives collapsed in June under pressure from the secularist army.
The Islamists are tipped to do well at the next elections but there are few accurate opinion polls.
